fixtures.preview: Michael Carrick's injury-hit United visit Madrid for matchday 2 of the Champions League league phase, looking for a response to Saturday's 1-1 draw with Spurs.
talking_points: Kobbie Mainoo and Luke Shaw did not travel after knocks against Spurs, and Sesko, Dorgu, Mazraoui and Ugarte are also out, per Carrick's pre-match press conference.
Matthijs de Ligt is back after an 11-month injury layoff and could come off the bench.
United are 13th in the Premier League on 6 points from 6 games (Sky Sports table, 12 Oct), but opened this Champions League campaign with a 4-0 win over Sabah.
Carrick said captain Bruno Fernandes has been playing through pain but has almost fully recovered; no injury is described as serious.

fixtures.preview: A Sunday 2pm Roses clash at Elland Road, with seventh-placed Leeds (9 points) hosting 13th-placed United (6 points) on Sky Sports' 12 October table.
A trip to Lake Como for matchday 3 of the Champions League league phase.
Sunday home game against 18th-placed Bournemouth (3 points), moved from Saturday for UK TV.
Lunchtime trip to Stamford Bridge to face sixth-placed Chelsea (10 points).
The A-League Men season opens with a Sydney Derby at Allianz Stadium, with former Sydney FC coach Ufuk Talay now in charge of the Wanderers.
talking_points: Talay, whom Sydney FC parted ways with in March, makes his first A-League appearance as Wanderers coach and returns to Allianz Stadium for the first time since.
Captain Rhyan Grant, who has played 36 matches against the Wanderers, says the rivalry is "as fierce as ever" and expects an electric atmosphere.
Both clubs have had big off-seasons of change; the Wanderers say Talay is building a side around intensity and discipline.
No confirmed team news or injury list had been published when this was written.

fixtures.preview: A Sunday-afternoon home game against Adelaide United with cheaper junior and family tickets.
Halloween 5pm game at AAMI Park, which is Melbourne City's official home opener.
Friday home game against the Mariners; the date comes from a fixture listing and the club hasn't confirmed the kick-off.
Away trip to Brisbane Roar at Kayo Stadium.

big_matches.title: Manchester City v Paris Saint-Germain
big_matches.why: Heavyweights meet at the Etihad on matchday 2, with PSG as reigning champions.
talking_points: City lead the Premier League on 18 points from 6 games (Sky Sports, 12 Oct) and beat Porto 2-0 on matchday 1; PSG hammered Slovan Bratislava 6-1.
Erling Haaland was substituted in Norway's Nations League game, so his fitness is being checked; other previews expect him to start.
PSG have reportedly failed to win on their last four visits to Manchester City.

notes: Man Utd: Mainoo, Shaw, Sesko, Dorgu, Mazraoui and Ugarte are reported out for Atlético, per Carrick's press conference as relayed by manutdnews. The Premier League table is Sky Sports' 12 Oct version; Man City's Haaland fitness is conflicting between previews. Kick-offs are in local time, so Manchester games use +01:00 until UK clocks change on 25 Oct.

Sydney FC: the derby is 7:45pm per the club. The Mariners game (6 Nov) appears only in fixture listings, not the club's home-ticket list, so its kick-off is unconfirmed; listings suggest around 7:40pm. No confirmed derby team news was found.

Big matches: no match-specific team news was found for PSG v Barcelona, Bayern v Arsenal or Atlético v Bayern, so they have no talking points. The Bledisloe broadcaster for Sydney isn't named in the article I opened, which only names Stan Sport and Nine for the Auckland Test; it is not listed under big matches for that reason.

Live sport: Kings and Flames start times come from an Austadiums listing, not the clubs. No Matildas, Socceroos, tennis or Waratahs games in Sydney were found for the next four weeks, and the Sydney FC v Mariners game was left out as unconfirmed.
Local: only three items found, all events. No Term 4 events were found for the schools, and nothing recent was found on local news, South Eveleigh or Sydney Park.

Not found this run: Pokémon, Minecraft or Roblox events in Sydney, junior fun runs beyond Triathlon Pink, matcha pop-ups (the one Mascot listing had no dates), Sydney deals on boots or running shoes (Rebel's sale ended 11 Oct), and ticket deals.

Groceries: Woolworths and Coles specials are from the 7–13 Oct trackers, so they end today (Tue 13 Oct). Several are brand ranges rather than exact items. New specials start Wed 14 Oct but weren't published yet, and ALDI's weekly specials couldn't be read.
